P517069.project_abstract: 1. Introduction: The Government of India is focusing on strengthening the core capacity of animal health system in India, including upgrading existing veterinary infrastructure such as diagnostic laboratories and facilities, veterinary hospitals and dispensaries, strengthening surveillance and disease reporting capacity, building capacity at community level and One Health coordination capacity. Strengthening Health Infrastructure for Livestock Disease Control Program (SHIELD) will be a subset of the larger government program and contribute to the overarching government Livestock Disease Control program (LHDCP) and will be implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying for over five years (2026-2031) as a 100 percent centrally sponsored national program. The overall LHDCP size is US$1.3 billion, of which the SHIELD Program boundary is US$162 million, to which the PforR will contribute US$81.123 million.2. Government Program: The DAHD is implementing an overarching animal health management program, namely the Livestock Health and Disease Control Program (LHDCP) for the period 2026-2031. The key objectives of the LHDCP are to maintain a healthy, disease-free livestock population, and control animal diseases including zoonotic diseases. The program contributes directly to India’s Viksit Bharat agenda through its contribution to farmer incomes, employment generation and entrepreneurship by improving animal health, and increasing livestock productivity and production. In addition, controlling zoonoses and increasing the capacity of disease management directly contributes to reducing the threat of future pandemics and related shocks. 3. The program consists of the following components (i) Critical Animal Disease Control Programme (CADCP) to control of Classical Swine Fever and Peste des Petits Ruminants; (ii) Establishment and Strengthening of Veterinary Hospitals, Dispensaries and Mobile Veterinary Units (ESVHD) to support operationalizations of Mobile Veterinary Units; (iii) Assistance to States for Control of Animal Diseases (ASCAD) that support surveillance and monitoring support important livestock and poultry diseases, vaccination of economically important animal diseases (livestock and poultry), control of emerging and exotic diseases, strengthening the Veterinary Council of India; (iv) National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) to support vaccination against priority livestock such as Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), Brucellosis, Classica Swine Fever (CSF) and Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR), and (v) National Digital Livestock Mission (NDLM) to support disease reporting, surveillance and (vi) Programme for Strengthening Health Infrastructure for Livestock Disease Control (SHIELD) focusing on improving district and state diagnostic facilities, block level veterinary hospitals and capacity building of veterinary institutions (to which World Bank SHIELD project will contribute).4. The government program has achieved significant results. Achievements include the vaccination of 1,391.72 million vaccinations against FMD covering around 316.5 million animals and the declaration of FMD-free zones in three states; immunization against other economically important diseases (Brucellosis, PPR, CSF and Lumpy Skin Diseases), and the initiation of a control program for classical swine fever in the northeastern regions. However, these achievements are constrained by various factors including poor diagnostic and surveillance capacity, veterinary human resource shortfall, poor disease reporting and surveillance, insufficient investment at community level to improve disease reporting and risks management. 5. The proposed PforR aims to support the government in implementing selected elements of the LHDCP, focusing on building system capacity for animal health management in an integrated, outcome-focused manner, as well as using a decentralized approach to strengthen disease surveillance at community level, enabling early disease detection, containment and strengthening the livestock economy. The Program will support subsets of the ASCAD, NDLM and SHIELD, and other areas of support will be refined during program preparation. In particular, the PforR will focus on strengthening the core capacity of animal health management, strengthen critical surveillance infrastructure, support community level awareness and training of veterinary professionals in all States and UTs to better prevent, detect and control animal disease outbreaks.6. The indicative expenditure framework for the overarching LHDCP government program (p”) for fiscal years 2026 to 2031 is US$1.3 billion. The Program (“P”), which forms part of the broader government program (“p”), has a defined expenditure boundary estimated at US$162 million over five years. Of this amount, the World Bank will provide US$81.123 million in financing, accounting for 50 percent of the program’s total budget. The Bank-supported PforR Program focuses on institutional capacity building, systems development to enhance disease diagnostic and surveillance, improving the quality and coverage of diagnostic and veterinary services and investment at community level for increasing awareness on good practices, disease reporting, risk management and One Health coordination. The PforR Program will exclude civil works related to the construction of new facilities, and procurement of vaccines. Civil works under the Program will include renovations and upgrading of existing physical infrastructure (e.g., veterinary hospitals, veterinary dispensaries, laboratories).7. CPF Alignment: The proposed Program aligns directly with the India Country Partnership Framework (FY26–31) through the following outcome areas: (1) Rural Resilience and Prosperity and Investing in People for Jobs-ready Workforce.  It contributes to CPF Outcome 1 on “Fostering prosperity and resilience for better opportunities in rural areas” through improving (i) infrastructure of veterinary services and diagnostic infrastructure critical to animal disease management and prevention which contributes to livestock production and productivity; (ii) supporting digital innovations to veterinary services and advisory service delivery, especially for rural households in remote areas. In addition, through (2) Outcome 3 on “Investing in people, for job ready workforce” through upgrading skills and strengthening health”. The program will support training and upskilling of livestock farmers on good animal husbandry practices, staff of identified livestock points (including livestock markets and abattoirs) on good handling practices, to improve biosecurity measures to reduce disease risks and improve livestock productivity.  In addition, the program will invest in the training and upskilling of para-veterinarians, laboratory personnel, field staff including forest department staff and livestock community extension workers. At the macro level these improvements can help increase livestock trade and improve access to disease-free animal protein.8. Jobs and Public Health: Livestock is one of India's largest rural employment generators. More than 70 percent of rural households derive some livelihood benefit from livestock, with the dairy sector alone engaging over 80 million farmers. The sector offers a major pathway for job creation, women's economic empowerment, income diversification, and rural transformation. Animal disease outbreaks can have far-reaching economic consequences beyond the livestock sector, specifically by disrupting agriculture, food processing, hospitality and manufacturing, among other sectors. Indirect costs, which are often overlooked, account for nearly half of the total losses, justifying greater public investment in disease prevention. The public health burden of zoonotic diseases can be enormous. P508565.project_abstract: The project will implement strategic pathways tailored to focus on enterprise promotion and job creation. The project will support (i) growth-oriented enterprises by strengthening the enabling ecosystem to crowd in private investment and generate employment. This includes improved access to organized markets, commercial finance, technology, and risk management instruments, and fostering enterprise networks, clusters, and priority value chain partnerships; (ii) aspiring entrepreneurs, particularly small and marginal farmers, women, and youth, with structured business development services, skills, mentoring, and access to productive assets and finance, enabling them to transition from vulnerability to stable and viable economic activity with income gains; and (iii) institutional and systems strengthening to enhance state and substate delivery capacity, community institutions, and digital platforms to improve targeting, coordination, and accountability, and to sustain private sector engagement at scale. These pathways will be implemented through the Tamil Nadu Rural Incubator and Startup Enabler (TN-RISE) under the Department of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj (RD&PR).

P515072.project_abstract: The proposed MPA Operation, MUWREP, will support the Government of Maharashtra in strengthening urban water supply and sanitation institutions, improving service delivery and wastewater reuse, and mobilizing private capital in participating cities. The Operation is designed as a hybrid PforR and IPF.  The Operation will support 35 urban local bodies across Maharashtra, covering large, medium, and smaller cities with varying institutional capacity, infrastructure needs, and financing readiness. The PforR will focus on large and medium municipal corporations, while the IPF component will support smaller municipal councils requiring integrated city-wide water and sanitation investments and implementation support. The Operation is expected to directly benefit more than 10 million people, with wider indirect benefits for over 30 million residents through improved governance, service delivery, wastewater management, and replicable financing models.The Program is organized around three pillars: strengthening institutions and policies for sustainable water supply, sanitation, and reuse; improving service delivery and resource efficiency through investments in water supply, sanitation, wastewater treatment, reuse, and renewable energy; and enhancing financial sustainability and access to private/commercial capital. Disbursement-linked indicators will incentivize state and city-level reforms, improved service outcomes, operational efficiency, financial performance, and private capital mobilization.A key feature of the Operation is its One World Bank Group blended financing approach, combining IBRD results-based financing, IFC investment and transaction advisory support, state and city contributions, commercial borrowing, pooled and municipal bonds, public-private partnerships, and land asset monetization. The Operation will support Maharashtra’s transition from infrastructure-led investments toward a more service-oriented, financially sustainable, and climate-resilient model for urban water supply and sanitation.

P500380.project_abstract: This project will implement an integrated and community-based local development planning process with the objective of improving livelihoods and housing for PVTG households. The project will start with community mobilization and facilitation of an inclusive, multisectoral planning process in select villages that is anchored in the broader annual Gram Panchayat (GP) development planning approach to identify key gaps in areas of convergence and systematically include the voices of PVTG households. P513529.project_abstract: India faces a significant infrastructure financing gap, estimated at 4–5 percent of GDP annually, or roughly US$160 billion per year above current spending levels. While the government finances approximately 78 percent of existing infrastructure investment, this falls well short of the 8–10 percent of GDP required to meet long-term development goals through 2047. Two structural constraints drive this shortfall: a limited pipeline of bankable, well-prepared projects on the demand side, and an underdeveloped intermediation ecosystem on the supply side that prevents long-term domestic savings - held by pension funds, insurance companies, and provident funds - from being effectively deployed into infrastructure. Foreign participation remains similarly constrained by currency risk, limited hedging instruments, and the absence of credible borrowing histories among many Indian financial institutions active in the sector.To address these gaps, the Government of India established the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) in 2021 as a dedicated development finance institution with a mandate to mobilize private and institutional capital, deepen bond markets, and reduce the rating and risk perception barriers that limit investor participation. NaBFID's balance sheet alone cannot close the financing gap, but it is strategically positioned to act as a catalytic platform - particularly through partial credit enhancement mechanisms that can multiply its impact by unlocking large pools of domestic patient capital without proportionately expanding public sector balance-sheet exposure. Supportive regulatory action by the RBI in August 2025, including raising permissible credit enhancement coverage from 20 to 50 percent of bond value and standardizing instrument structures, has meaningfully strengthened the enabling environment for this approach.Project UPLIFT operationalizes this vision by supporting NaBFID in launching a Credit Enhancement Facility (CEF) that provides irrevocable, subordinated, contingent credit support to eligible infrastructure bond issuers, thereby elevating their credit ratings into investment-grade territory and broadening access to long-tenor institutional capital. The World Bank Group - through IBRD loans and guarantees, alongside a MIGA Non-Honoring of Financial Obligations guarantee and parallel ADB financing - backstops CEF exposures, lowers regulatory capital requirements, and supports access to international investors. This "One WBG" approach is designed to crowd in private domestic and foreign capital at scale, lower borrowing costs, and extend debt maturities in line with infrastructure asset lives, directly advancing India's growth agenda while operationalizing the Country Partnership Framework's leveraging bank model.

P517113.project_abstract: (1) Context and Key IssuesKarnataka, India’s ninth most populous state (69 million in 2026), and has above-average urbanization (38.7%), with urban growth highly concentrated in major centers, most notably in the State capital- Bengaluru.  Private vehicle growth—particularly cars and two-wheelers at ~10%—has outpaced state-owned bus services, which expanded at only ~2% Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR). This divergence has created a widening gap between demand and formal public transport supply. The three regional RTCs - Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC), Northwestern Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (NWKRTC), and Kalyana Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (KKRTC) operate about 19,000 buses serving rural, semi-urban and intercity/ interstate routes, whereas in Bengaluru, the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC), urban RTC operates 7,000 buses. Buses account for 41% of all non-agricultural work trips and are particularly critical for women and low-income populations. However:• Access gaps persist in rural areas, with many villages lacking direct bus connectivity.• Urban congestion and emissions are rising due to rapid motorization, increasing travel times and costs. The challenge extends beyond fleet size to fleet composition and modernization:• Electric bus (e-bus) adoption is concentrated in Bengaluru (~25% of fleet), with minimal uptake in other regions.• Depot and charging infrastructure remain inadequate, and RTCs lack technical capacity for e-bus system management.• Shift to Gross Cost Contracts (GCC) requires RTCs to transition from operators to performance-oriented contract managers. Financial and institutional constraints have compounded these issues:• High input costs, below cost recovery fares, operational inefficiencies, and COVID-19 impacts have led to accumulated losses and declining creditworthiness.• RTCs rely on discretionary state support, limiting access to commercial finance and private sector participation.• Fragmented institutional systems and weak data integration hinder route rationalization, service optimization, and demand-responsive planning. (2) Program DescriptionIn 2022, the Government of Karnataka (GoK) adopted a strategic roadmap to transform RTCs into financially sustainable and operationally efficient public transport providers, identifying 21 reform areas. The program is anchored on three pillars:1. Improving operational efficiency and financial sustainability2. Expanding urban and regional bus services (with ~50% private participation)3. Strengthening institutional frameworks and capacity The proposed Karnataka Bus Reforms for Efficiency, Electrification & Sustainability (K-BREEZE) PforR operation supports a targeted subset of activities aligned with this roadmap, organized around three interrelated results areas (RAs):• Improving operational efficiency and financial sustainability of RTCs  o Introduce a performance-linked financial architecture, replacing ad hoc subsidies with Public Transport Service Contracts (PTSCs)  o Establish transparent fare revision mechanisms to improve cost recovery and fiscal predictability • Creating and Enabling Ecosystem for Private Sector Participation in Bus Service Delivery   o Develop bankable contractual frameworks through standardized GCCs supported by a Liquidity Support Facility (LSF)  o Improve risk allocation to enable private operators and lenders to scale investments in fleet expansion, especially e-buses  o Expand depot and charging infrastructure to enable fleet electrification • Institutional strengthening and capacity building:  o Support RTCs’ transition from fleet operators to professional contract managers  o Upgrade technical capabilities, digital systems, and planning functions(3) Strategic AlignmentK-BREEZE is closely aligned with the India Country Partnership Framework (CPF) FY2026–2031 and the Government’s Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.The operation supports private sector led job creation:• Generate ~40,000 direct and indirect jobs across operations, manufacturing, and services• Create significant opportunities for private operators, lenders, and International Finance Corporation (IFC) - World Bank Group's private sector lending arm. IFC can mobilize large scale debt and equity capital into the bus market, as this operation would create enabling ecosystem for private sector participation through improving contractual bankability and creditworthiness. • Mobilize large-scale investment into sustainable mobilityIt directly contributes to the CPF outcomes:• Outcome 1: Rural Prosperity and Resilience  o Expands bus connectivity to underserved villages  o Improves access to jobs and markets, boosting local economic activity • Outcome 2: Urban Development  o Enhances urban mobility through scaled private investment  o Improves air quality and reduces congestion  o Strengthens Bengaluru’s role as an economic growth hub • Outcome 3: Investing in People  o Builds a job-ready workforce through institutionalized skill development  o Supports workforce transition to new technologies and service models The operation is designed under the CPF’s “Budget-Plus” and “Finance-Plus” approaches:• Catalyzing private capital through Public Private Partnerships (PPPs)• Combining financing with global knowledge, digitalization, and skill development• Driving system-wide transformation rather than incremental improvements  It also aligns with the WBG Climate Change Action Plan by promoting low-emission transport (e-buses) and supporting climate mitigation and adaptation outcomes.
P517113.impagency: Transport Department, State Government of Karnataka
P517113.project_name: K-BREEZE: Karnataka Bus Reforms for Efficiency, Electrification & Sustainability Operation

P512959.project_abstract: The Bihar Rural Transformation Project (BRTP, P512959) is a INR 3000 crore (US$312.5M) operation, financed through an IBRD loan of INR 2100 crore (US$218.8M) and INR 900 crore (US$93.7M) in Government of Bihar counterpart funding. The Project Development Objective is to support more and better-paid jobs, and improve health and nutrition outcomes. Implemented by the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS), popularly known as JEEViKA, the project builds on nearly two decades of World Bank engagement in Bihar and leverages JEEViKA's network of 10 million Self-Help Group members to drive a more ambitious agenda of market-oriented rural economic transformation.The project is structured around four components. Component A integrates smallholder producers into value chains through productive partnerships with private sector off-takers and builds an ecosystem of three million rural enterprises, with a focus on graduating enterprises from own-account to hired worker status. Component B  establishes three state-level apex institutions, a Marketing Federation, an Enterprise Anchor Facility, and a Shared Service Organization, and strengthens community institutions as platforms for health, nutrition, and climate resilience. Component C addresses financing and digital market failures through matching grants, a blended finance instrument, insurance products, and an AI-enabled Bihar Rural Stack. Component D covers project management, monitoring and evaluation, and knowledge partnerships. The project is expected to support approximately 773,000 more and better-paid jobs, benefit 3 million entrepreneurs, and reach 1.2 million women and 170,000 children through a community resilience and convergence model in 200 Cluster Level Federations.

P510062.project_abstract: The Gurugram Metro (Millennium City Center to Cyber City) focuses on enhancing urban public transport by developing the proposed Gurugram metro rail. It is the first project of a proposed Series of Project (SOP) developing a hierarchical and integrated transport system at three-levels to promote spatially balanced regional development and support Haryana's growth. The first level focuses on enhancing urban public transport in major cities starting from Gurugram Metro (from Millennium City Center to Cyber City) (SOP-1), integrated with expanded metro network and electric buses in (SOP-2), will also be supported by the World Bank (WB) under the Haryana Clean Air Project (P510686). The second level aims at improving regional connectivity between major economic hubs and their peripheral towns within a 150 km radius, as exemplified by the Delhi-SNB and Delhi Karnal regional rail corridors (SOP-3). The third level emphasizes the importance of intercity transport (SOP-4) to connect small-medium size cities with each other as well as with the major cities, with a significant role for buses to boost economic activities, facilitate access to jobs and services, and promote inclusive growth, by providing safe and accessible services to all, including vulnerable populations.The Gurugram Metro Rail project (SOP-1) consists of four components: Component 1: Develop a world-class metrorail system. This component will finance the construction of the elevated metro line in Gurugram to provide the backbone infrastructure of mass transit system in the city including i) In two packages, including the first civil works contract (viaduct structure of 15.5km and main structure of 14 stations) already under construction and financed by GMRL’s own funding  and the IBRD-financed second contract, consisting of viaducts structure of 13.5km, main structures of 13 stations, Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) and architectural finishing of all 27 stations. The stations will incorporate features of deploying solar panel to generate energy for use in the station, user friendly and inclusive station design and finishing, as well as climate resilient facilities against flooding and extreme heat; ii) Rolling stocks; and iii) Systems of traction and power supply, telecommunication, signaling, Automatic Fare Collection (AFC), lifts and escalators, digital system provides integrated services information (routes, fare, availability), and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC). Component 2: Maximize ridership and farebox revenues. This component will finance i) Multimodal Integration (MMI) infrastructure within the stations' within the stations’ right of way (RoW); and ii) First -Last Mile (FLM) services (through private sector, no additional project cost).Component 3: Capitalize of GMRL and project management. This component will support i) GMRL to utilize the resources provided under this component to increase the attractiveness to raise financing from DFIs and/or CBs through a sequenced financing approach; and ii) supporting GMRL in its daily operations, such as construction management, technical operations, procurement management, monitoring and evaluation, E&S compliance, and relevant areas to achieve the PDO.
P510062.project_name: Gurugram Metro Rail Project - Sustainable Multimodal and Resilient Transport for Haryana

P508453.project_abstract: Despite its abundant natural resources, Meghalaya faces challenges such as inadequate transport connectivity and inefficient logistics infrastructure and services that have resulted in limited market access for local products, wastage of agricultural produce, and high logistics costs. The transport challenges in the state are due to a complex combination of inadequate funds and their inefficient use, low institutional effectiveness, difficult hilly terrain, and extreme climatic conditions. The state aims to significantly increase agriculture's economic contribution and per capita income through better access to markets via an efficient, all-weather transport and logistics infrastructure and services network that enhances logistics efficiency along key economic corridors connecting Meghalaya's growth centers. The implementation of the core initiatives of the project is expected to result in: a.	Enhanced connectivity to key growth centers along identified road corridors b.	Improved rural and district-level logistics infrastructure and servicesc.	Greater market access and reduced average cost/time for select agriculture and horticulture products to reach the marketsd.	Strengthened institutional capacity for efficient, climate-resilient transport and logisticse.	(Millions of) direct users that benefit from improved access to sustainable transport infrastructure and services (Corporate Scorecard)

P517479.project_abstract: The proposed operation is part of the World Bank-financed Regional Air Quality Management (AQM) Program in the Indo-Gangetic Plain and Himalayan Foothills (IGP-HF) region, which supports Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, and Pakistan in institutional strengthening, emissions reduction, and regional knowledge exchange, forming the foundation of airshed management across the region. In India, the IGP covers around 18 percent of the country's land area and nearly 40 percent of its population, where rapid urbanization and economic growth have driven substantial emissions from transport, industry, road dust, and construction activities, making it a global air pollution hotspot. The Program aligns with India's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), India's Nationally Determined Contribution commitments, and interstate airshed directives from the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM).The CAQM estimated the source contributions through a meta-analysis of emissions inventory studies from 2015 to 2025 that were available for Delhi or data shared by a panel of experts convened by CAQM in Identification of the causes for worsening AQI in Delhi National Capital Region (NCR), Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas, January 2026 (CAQM, 2026). Delhi has implemented one of India’s most comprehensive air pollution control programs, combining policy reforms, enforcement measures, infrastructure investments, and sectoral interventions. The government’s commitment is reflected in the Delhi Air Pollution Mitigation Action Plan (DAPMP) 2026 and the allocation of a Green Budget of US$2.4 billion (21.44% of total Government of National Capital of Delhi (GNCTD) budget for FY 2026-27) for mainstreaming environmental considerations in government planning and expenditure. However, the complexity of managing emissions across sectors and jurisdictions—particularly given the transboundary nature of sources and evolving meteorological influences—requires strengthened coordination, implementation consistency, and evidence-based decision-making.DCAP Phase 1 is part of a proposed seven-year Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA), supporting the GNCTD with successive financing operations to manage the complexity of cross-sector interventions and build sustained air quality management systems. The phased approach enables sequencing—from immediate emission reduction actions to longer-term investments and structural reforms—while incorporating learning and scaling across phases.  Phase 1 of the Program would focus on: (i) short- to medium-term actions to reduce air pollution in major sources of PM2.5 emissions - transport and road dust; and (ii) development of a long-term AQM plan and its corresponding institutional framework. Subsequent phases are expected to scale and deepen these interventions and expand support to additional sectors and strengthen policy frameworks based on emerging evidence and priorities for sustained air quality improvements. DCAP Phase 1 would finance a Program for Results (PforR) combined with technical assistance to support GNCTD’s multi-sector effort across four results areas (RAs): 1)	Strengthening AQM Planning, ,Coordination and Citizen Engagement: Global experience demonstrates that a robust AQM framework is crucial to achieving sustained, measurable clean air improvements. Delhi has established an extensive policy and regulatory foundation, as well as a dense air quality monitoring network, which provide a strong platform for further consolidation. Opportunities remain to strengthen multi-sector planning, improve data quality and integration, develop more effective policies and financing instruments, update emissions inventories, and enhance monitoring, enforcement, and inter-agency coordination for enhanced implementation and enforcement of clean air initiatives. A well-designed and sustained communications and behaviour change strategy can also strengthen public awareness, encourage behavioural shifts, and foster broader stakeholder engagement. The first phase would support the GNCTD: (i) develop and start implementing a medium-term Delhi Air Pollution Management Plan (DAPMP) 2027-2031, including defined targets, budget, governance framework and M&E systems; (ii) set up the institutional arrangements of DAPMP, and (iii) design and deploy a strategic communications plan.2)	Reducing Emissions from Transport: Transport plays a significant and complex role in Delhi NCR's air quality crisis, acting as a major year-round contributor to pollution. Transport emissions account for an estimated 19–23% of primary PM2.5 concentrations and 81%  of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions in Delhi (CAQM 2026) which is a precursor of secondary particulate matter contributing to PM2.5. Rapid and sustained growth in the vehicle fleet, coupled with significant daily traffic inflows from neighbouring NCR cities—including a high share of heavy-duty diesel vehicles (trucks and buses) that contribute disproportionately to particulate matter emissions—has intensified the problem. This is further exacerbated by the prevalence of older and poorly maintained vehicles with weak emission controls, resulting in real-world emissions that often exceed certified standards. Systematic solutions to decouple growth in transport demand from emissions, while transitioning towards cleaner vehicles, could significantly reduce transport emissions. While electrification presents a major opportunity for emission reduction, the pace of transition is constrained by gaps in charging infrastructure, including inadequate charger density, uneven spatial distribution of charging stations, limited charging options for commercial and heavy-duty vehicles, and challenges related to land availability and grid connectivity. The first phase interventions for transport sector would focus on strengthening enforcement systems, enabling conditions for scaled transition to cleaner and public transport. Key activities would include (i) enhancing enforcement mechanisms to limit entry and operation of high emitting (pre-BS VI vehicles) and end-of-life vehicles; (ii) accelerating implementation of Delhi’s upcoming EV Policy 2.0 and rollout of charging infrastructure; (iii) strengthening the electric bus (e-bus) ecosystem through bus service optimization and depot infrastructure readiness; (iv) creating an inter-agency coordination mechanism for integrated planning and delivery of mobility services in the city.3)	Reducing Emissions from Road Dust: Road dust is recognized as a major contributor to particulate pollution, particularly in dense urban environments with extensive road networks and ongoing construction activity. Emissions from soil, road and C&D dust within Delhi NCR and beyond account for 15% to 27% of primary PM2.5 concentration in Delhi in winter and summer, respectively (CAQM 2026). Delhi's road network spans an estimated 16,040 lane-km, is managed across multiple agencies with distinct mandates - including the Public Works Department (PWD), the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC), as well as the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) and 9 other agencies.  This distributed structure requires strengthened coordination across agencies for minimizing dust generation from repeated construction activity on same streets and effective implementation of dust control measures. There is an opportunity to expand vacuum sweeping with close performance monitoring across greater share of Delhi’s road network, while strengthening coordinated planning and asset management across agencies to reduce repeated excavation and improve road conditions.Strategic Alignment to CPF. DCAP is closely aligned with the India CPF FY2026-2031 and with the vision for a Viksit Bharat 2047. The operation would address a critical challenge identified in the CPF - poor air quality - and support the CPF’s emphasis on improved livability, sustainability

P513815.project_abstract: Cloudbursts, flash floods and landslide incidents triggered by heavy rain during the 2025 monsoon season (June to date) have caused extensive impacts in Himachal Pradesh, resulting in about 486 deaths and damages/losses estimated at US$653 million. Damages are primarily driven by impacts to the transport infrastructure, public buildings, power infrastructure, and water, sanitation and irrigation, while the livelihood sector additionally faces significant indirect losses due to disrupted access to markets, significant reduction of tourist arrivals etc. These events follow similarly devastating monsoon seasons in 2023 and 2024. These repeated extreme weather events have severely strained the state’s already constrained capacities, and substantial recovery needs from 2023 and 2024 remain unmet emphasizing the urgency of a speedy and resilient reconstruction and recovery effort. The proposed project will support the Government of Himachal Pradesh in advancing a resilient recovery process (transport corridors, public buildings, water/sanitation/irrigation schemes, and energy supply) while strengthening institutional capacities for disaster risk management, enhancing sectoral resilience for infrastructure sectors and supporting resilient livelihoods.

P510002.project_abstract: The project focuses on upgrading 360 km of damaged roads with climate-resilient features to mitigate flooding and landslides. It includes widening roads, stabilizing slopes using civil and bioengineering methods, enhancing drainage and bridge structures, and developing alternative escape routes. Rehabilitation efforts will involve pavement reconstruction and drainage improvements, supported by Performance-Based Maintenance Contracts and various consultancy services. Additionally, an electronic Project Management System will be implemented for real-time monitoring, alongside Road User Satisfaction Surveys and technical advisory support from academic institutions. The project will introduce a digital system for real-time inspection and monitoring of road works, alongside an institutional review to strengthen Assam’s Road Safety Lead Agency. Work zone safety will be integrated throughout, with an independent road safety audit ensuring best practices.The project aims to develop a green rural freight and public transportation system by establishing rural logistics hubs equipped with EV charging stations, solar-powered infrastructure, and amenities like workshops, refreshment areas, and transport bays. It includes a freight terminal linked to a district industrial park, demonstration ropeways for farm produce, and georeferenced transport stations with high-speed internet. Additional facilities include packaging, storage, sanitation, and roadside marketplaces. The project focuses on enhancing climate resilience and disaster preparedness in road infrastructure. It includes developing a climate adaptation framework/policy through multi-hazard risk analysis, integrating structural and bioengineering solutions into road design and maintenance. A Flood and Landslide Early Warning System (FLEWS) will be established to improve monitoring, forecasting, and communication with road users and communities, integrated into APWRD’s Road Asset Management System. Additionally, institutional capacity will be strengthened through the formulation of a robust transport emergency management and response plan to ensure rapid recovery after disasters.
P510002.project_name: Assam Disaster Resilient Hill Roads Development Project (ADRHRDP)

P505190.project_abstract: Bihar, despite its fertile lands in the Indo-Gangetic Plain, faces significant challenges in water management, with inconsistent monsoons, inadequate irrigation, frequent flooding, and drought severely limiting agricultural productivity and economic growth. This project aims to address these issues through two key interventions: improving irrigation systems and enhancing flood and erosion control. Using Investment Project Financing (IPF) and Performance-Based Conditions (PBCs), the project seeks to transform Bihar’s water management sector and ensure long-term sustainability.The project comprises four components, addressing both environmental and social concerns. Component 1 focuses on restoring and modernizing irrigation infrastructure without disturbing the river’s main stem or the flow in the river. This will optimize water availability, reduce losses, and promote efficient water use, supporting climate-resilient agriculture. Component 2 tackles flood risk reduction by strengthening existing embankments. The project will not finance the construction of new embankments, instead observed damages in stretches of embankments and riverbanks that are affecting the protection of canal infrastructure, and the command irrigation area will be strengthened. This approach minimizes environmental disruption while protecting communities and irrigation infrastructure from future flood and drought risks. The project will also explore green infrastructure such as nature-based solutions.Component 3 strengthens water governance and institutional frameworks by implementing operational procedures, testing new irrigation service models, and expanding early warning systems for floods and droughts. Component 4 ensures effective project execution through monitoring and evaluation, integrating climate co-benefits, gender inclusivity, and citizen engagement. The project aligns with World Bank policies, addressing potential social impacts, such as the presence of squatters, while promoting equitable and sustainable outcomes. Together, these interventions aim to modernize Bihar’s water management, enhancing agricultural productivity and community resilience.
P505190.impagency: Water Resources Department (WRD), Government of Bihar
P505190.project_name: Bihar Water Security and Irrigation Modernization Project

P180932.project_abstract: The development objective of the Strengthening Coastal Resilience and the Economy Project for India is to increase the resilience of targeted coastal communities and ecosystems. The project comprises of six components. The first component, strengthening institutions for integrated coastal zone management will support Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to plan, analyze, and make decisions about the management of their coastal and marine resources through the provision of consulting services, training and goods. The second component, shoreline management, coastal protection, and conservation will enhance the resilience of physical and natural coastal assets. The third component, improving livelihoods for natural resource dependent communities will support coastal communities in the participating states to create and sustain climate-resilient livelihoods and will finance consulting services, community grants, goods, works, and training. The fourth component, enhancing marine pollution management and plastic circularity will provide support to reduce the threats to marine and coastal resources from plastic pollution through financing of upstream and downstream interventions in identified hotspots. The fifth component, project management will support development of Project management and monitoring systems and strengthening the capacity of the State Project Management Unit (SPMUs) to implement the Project, including the provision of support. The sixth component, contingent emergency response component will provide immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed, by reallocating uncommitted loan proceeds from the other components.

P180699.project_abstract: The Government of Tamil Nadu (GoTN) implements a multi-sector program that focuses on women’s economic empowerment through skill building, enterprise support, infrastructure development, and service delivery interventions. Complementing the state’s economic vision, the Tamil Nadu Women’s Policy (2021, draft) puts forward a comprehensive plan for women’s empowerment. The proposed PforR Program, Tamil Nadu Women Employment and Safety (WeSafe) will support a subset of the government program to improve women’s access to quality jobs in non-farm and emerging sectors. Traditional government programming on women’s employment has adopted a sector-specific delivery approach; either through skill development, rural livelihoods, entrepreneurship promotion, or school-to-work transition related interventions. The WeSafe Program proposes an alternate, integrated programming approach to address bottlenecks that impede women’s access to quality jobs through: (i) strengthening state-level planning capacities via the state-led platform on women’s employment and district-led women’s quality employment plans; (ii) promoting targeted skilling and entrepreneurship support linked to emerging sectors; and (iii) improving delivery of enabling services in women’s safety, affordable housing, and care.The Program will support three Result Areas (RAs) that will contribute towards the achievement of the Program Development Objective.1.	RA 1: EMPLOY: Improved labor market performance for women in emerging sectors: Result Area 1 introduces an outcome-driven approach to enhance the relevance, accessibility, quality, and efficiency of skills training and entrepreneurship support for women in Tamil Nadu.2.	RA 2: ENABLE: Enhanced delivery of enabling services to promote women’s employment: Under Results Area 2, the Program will support setting up an investment framework to improve coordinated outreach, quality, and impact of enabling services particularly safety/violence prevention in public places and workplaces, affordable housing options, and care services.3.	RA 3: EMPOWER: Strengthened state capacities, technical partnerships, and institutional structures for women’s employment: Under Results Area 3, the state will develop a common results framework to support the roll-out of the state’s women policy and directly contribute to the state’s economic goal of achieving a trillion-dollar economic status. The Program will support setting-up of a state-led platform for women’s employment.
P180699.project_name: Tamil Nadu Women Employment and Safety (TN WESAFE) Operation

P179935.project_abstract: The objective of the Enhancing Landscape and Ecosystem Management (ELEMENT) Project for India is to improve landscape management and increase benefits for targeted forest dependent communities in Tripura and Nagaland. There are five components to the project, the first component being strengthening capacities for integrated landscape management. This component includes four subcomponents: strengthening the capacity of participating states relevant institutions in participatory planning, implementation, and monitoring; strengthening capacity of participating states institutions for Research and Development (R&D) and value chain development; Strengthening the capacity of existing and new community institutions for decentralized natural resources management; and knowledge and information sharing on innovation. The second component is the restoring landscapes for improved ecosystem services. This component includes two subcomponents: developing community landscape management plans, and implementation of community landscape management plans in targeted catchments. The third component is the enhancing landscape-based value-chains for economic transformation. This component includes two subcomponents: agroforestry, forestry, and NTFP in value chain development and forest landscape enterprises and augmenting eco-tourism opportunities. The fourth component is the project management, monitoring, and evaluation.  Finally, the fifth component is the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC). Provision of immediate response to an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, as needed. This will include reallocation of loan proceeds from other components to provide immediate response (which may include recovery and reconstruction support) following an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.

P178254.project_abstract: The project aims to address the main challenges hindering Kerala’s agriculture food system transition as part of the State's continued structural transformation. It will focus on addressing three main themes: (i) promoting resilience to climate change and contributing to India's mitigation targets; (ii) enhancing smallholder commercialization for value addition; and (iii) strengthening the private sector's role within the food system, especially MSMEs. Project interventions in these three main areas will focus on: (i) supporting resilience and adaptation through strengthening the extension system to promote an improved package of practices of climate smart agricultural technologies relevant to specific agroecological conditions (including integrated pest management to respond to changing disease vectors), and delivering climate change mitigation results by focusing on reducing emissions in paddy production, primarily through the adoption of alternative wet and dry (AWD) production techniques, as well as measures to improve fertilizer efficiency and other opportunities to promote the decarbonization of value chains including energy efficient storage facilities; (ii) facilitating productive alliances between small-holder farmers (individually or more likely via farmer producer companies [FPCs] to promote value addition and diversification into higher-value crop production, providing on-farm or community-level value chain infrastructure such as storage facilities and equipment to promote value addition, and support to farmer organizations, etc; and (iii) providing training and partial grants to existing MSMEs as part of a coherent and targeted hand-holding service, support to relevant agri-tech start-ups, and support to food/ agri-parks of various sizes to facilitate the clustering of competitive agro-processing.Project activities entail a mix of technical assistance type of support in the form of promotion and demonstration of new technologies including high-yield varieties and diversification into high-value commodities, as well as small-scale irrigation practices to enhance access to water and efficient use. It may support the provision of input packages directly such as seeds and will provide technical assistance to link farmers with input markets. The project will work with established FPCs to help them increase their capacity for aggregation, value addition and business management. Project activities may entail physical upgrades/ improvements to localized and small-scale irrigation systems, facilities for hygiene and waste management, and existing aggregation facilities (local farmer markets), including potential construction of warehouses and cold storage depending on the need and feasibility, and without requiring land acquisition. The project will also promote productivity in smallholder agriculture, which is expected to intensify farming activity, which would increase water usage and may result in an increased (albeit more efficient) use of fertilizers and pesticides by farmers. However, the project will not finance the purchase of inputs such as these. The project will provide technical assistance to existing agriculture and food sector MSMEs and small-scale agri parks, and also support an initial feasibility study for a new large-scale agri-park. Technical assistance to small-scale agri parks may also entail small-scale and localized physical upgrades/ improvements and construction on existing agri-park parcels. The project will also leverage commercial financing for plantations and smallholders, through the establishment of a Partial Risk Guarantee. The project will also support the ongoing reconfiguration of the DoA’s institutional structure and help strengthen coordination among key program and service delivery agencies with a goal of delivering agriculture support services effectively and efficiently. Project activities will primarily entail capacity building including procurement and use of digital technologies for advisory information dissemination as well as equipment and goods to facilitate mobility of extension workers to reach remote areas. Additionally, the project will also support development of new mechanisms for land consolidation through increased collective decision-making supported by policy and institutional measures to support land leasing.
P178254.impagency: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Kerala
P178254.project_name: Kerala Climate Resilient Agri- Value Chain Modernization (KERA) Project

P181195.project_abstract: India has made very significant development progress in recent decades and is expected to remain on an ascendent trajectory: its aspirations to become a high-income economy by 2047 would require it to elevate its rate of growth even further. From 1991 to today, the size of the economy has multiplied more than ten times, and gross domestic product (GDP) per capita seven times. From 1993-2022, the extreme poverty rate declined from 48 percent to 12.9 percent, reducing the number of extreme poor people by about 262 million. India’s past achievements set the tone for its future ambitions, notably the target to reach high income by 2047, which will require the economy to grow at 8 percent per annum on average over the next two decades. The actions supported under the proposed operation reflect India’s resolute and pragmatic approach to addressing climate change challenges. India’s policymakers are attempting to strike a complex balance between multiple objectives that entail inherent tradeoffs: boosting growth and innovation, including through targeted industrial policies; achieving energy security; and, contributing to global climate change objectives. Providing secure and affordable energy supply is a top priority for the GoI, with coal remaining the cheapest baseload supply available. The GoI’s drive to promote domestic manufacturing through “Make in India” will boost domestic productive capacity in RE, but it pushes up RE costs in the short-to-medium term, potentially delaying the large-scale adoption of RE. India’s policymakers are also trying to maximize the leveraging of public spending to crowd in the private sector and domestic commercial financing resources by providing just enough support to elicit private sector interest and drive down the cost curves, while optimizing the use of public resources.
P181195.impagency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

P177965.project_abstract: DAKSH Maharashtra supports the skills reform agenda in Maharashtra and aims to improve training and entrepreneurship for market-led employment. P179749.project_abstract: The objective of the Uttarakhand Disaster Preparedness and Resilience Project for India is to enhance the climate and disaster resilience of critical public infrastructure and strengthen disaster risk management capacity in Uttarakhand. The project has five components. (1) Enhancing Infrastructure Resilience component will support the development of climate- and disaster-resilient priority infrastructure and integrate resilience into infrastructure planning. (2) Improving Emergency Preparedness and Response component will support improving the capabilities of Uttarakhand’s government entities and first responders to predict, prepare for, and respond to disasters. (3) Preventing and Managing Forest and General Fires component will support enhancing the capacity of the Uttarakhand government and local communities to prevent and manage forest and general fires. (4)  Project Management component will support project management and knowledge sharing. (5) Contingent Emergency Response Component component will allow provision of immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed, through the reallocation of undisbursed loan proceeds.

P179749.project_name: Uttarakhand Disaster Preparedness and Resilience Project

P179357.project_abstract: The project will work towards (i) reduction of net GHG emission relative to control villages with similar cropping pattern; (ii) achievement of resilience of production systems by adopting precision-farming techniques; and (iii) increased profitability through enhanced productivity, reduced cost of cultivation, and additional income through carbon credits. An integrated digital platform for evidence-based decision-making will support the project activities. The project will focus on small and marginal farmers, including women farmers, and landless households. The project will be implemented in 1,226 villages covering a catchment area of 243,418 hectares (ha), which includes arable and non-arable land.
P179357.impagency: Watershed Management Directorate, Government of Uttarakhand
P179357.project_name: Uttarakhand Climate Responsive Rainfed Farming Project

P178581.project_abstract: The PforR Program’s boundary is restricted to improving bridges on the rural roads network – “rural bridges”. The Program interventions include: (a) maintenance; (b) widening single lane bridges; (c) replacement of temporary, distressed and collapsed/washed out bridges, and construction of new bridges; and (d) updating Electric Vehicle Policy to enhance rural e- mobility & establishing Green Rural Freight and Public Transportation Hubs along the rural roads network. The Program supports extensive resilience and institutional building initiatives with four process DLIs, including (e) enhancing resilience of bridges; (f) strengthening Environmental and Social management capability; (g) strengthening APWRD’s financial and procurement capability; and (h) strengthening roads and bridges management capability. IPF Component (TA Component) includes:a)	Prepare Program rural bridges investment and manage Program implementation, including Detail Project Report (DPR), Construction Supervision Consultants (CSC), Transport hub design, GRS, Gender Action Plan, and E&S impact managementb)	Program management support, studies, and system upgrading including Independent Verification Agent, Program Management Consultant, Technical Audit Consultant, Individual Consultants, Impact evaluation, training, road financing strategy, systems upgrading/development, studies; and administrative, legal, and operating expenses.c)	Strengthen the Assam Road Research and Training Institute (ARRTI) - center of excellence-, including training material development, delivering induction training and short-term courses, and research. This TA component is designed to achieve Disbursement Linked Indicator (DLI) #1 and the Program Action Plan (PAP) on environment and social risk management included in the PforR Operation. This is to address the gaps identified by the Environmental and Social Systems Assessment (ESSA) undertaken to assess the country systems and capacity of Institutions to effectively manage E&S risks. The DLI #1 covers:(i)	Adoption of Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) and Environmental and Social Policy - Indigenous People Policy (ESP-IPP)  that aligns with country laws and good international industry practices (GIIP) [The ESP-IPP and RPF including improved systems and procedures supported by the PforR will subsequently apply to the whole of government’s program. The ESP-IPP/RPF will include the screening criteria to avoid financing of any High E&S risk subprojects under Bank’s Program]; (ii)	Setting up of a dedicated E&S management unit that will report to planning and finance wings of the APWRD; and (iii)	Establishment of digital system to track compliance of the policies on real time basis. The DLI#1 is incentivized with a total sum of US$ 4.8 million (Scalable).The PAP is designed to ensure that civil works are initiated only after the client provides encumbrance free land in accordance with the ESP-IPP and RPF to the contractors before the commencement of the works. Both the DLI and PAP will be adopted sector wide by the Department. The Verification Agency will be expected to follow the verification protocol to the compliance of the PAP and the DLI. The TA component will support the (i) preparation of sub-project level ESIAs/ESMPs in accordance with the APWRD’s ESP-IPP that aligns with the national/state legal policy requirements and international standards, including the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) supported by PforR; (ii) set up the Grievance Management Systems; (iii) develop and implement the capacity building program of APWRD by the ESMU; (iv) prepare the Gender Action Plan; (v) implement the systems for evidence based monitoring for evidence based reporting supported under the PforR.

P176733.project_abstract: The proposed Project will address the gaps in the foundations of the digital economy of Manipur and invest in individuals and businesses to enable new sources of economic growth in the state.Component 1: Digital Industry, Skills, and JobsThe Project will finance activities to promote Manipur as an investment destination for digital industries. It will also support digital entrepreneurs and start-ups to create new engines of economic growth and jobs, including through development and implementation of entrepreneurship and innovation services, building on ongoing efforts of the GoM with the private sector. And the Project will support improved access to advanced digital skills and to digital employment opportunities for individuals while positioning the state as a hub for digital skills development in the NER. Component 2: Broadband Connectivity, Access, and UseActivities include supporting regulatory measures and a clearance system to implement the right-of-way policy and broadband cost reduction at the state level. The Project will finance investments that complement ongoing GoI initiatives, focusing on leapfrogging Manipur to next generation 5G technologies. Specifically, the Project will support Manipur becoming a testbed for this emerging suite of technologies and applications. The Project will also support digital literacy training, including basic digital skills, online business development, cybersecurity awareness, and online safety for the youth, women, and people living in villages/or hill districts. The Project will also finance small goods and services to provide select groups of beneficiaries of digital literacy programs with broadband services and devices. In line with the overall objectives of the Project, beneficiaries will be households with schoolchildren, women-headed households, and households that include persons with disabilities.Component 3: Foundations of Digital GovernmentThe Project will support the upgrade and capacity enhancement of the state data center (DC) and cloud services for the public sector. It will also finance a range of activities to cascade national policies and programs related to cybersecurity (CS) and data regulation to the state level across ministries, departments, and agencies. This Component will support improvements in the broader data regulation and trust ecosystem. And it will finance consultancies to re-design and deploy specific digital G2B services, including to develop an (online) one-stop-shop for investment into the digital industries, to develop a state-level skills registry for employees and job seekers in the IT and related industries, and to support establishment of digital startups. Component 4: Project Management and Coordination
P176733.project_name: IN: Manipur Infotech eNabled Development Project

P179337.project_abstract: The development objective of the Assam State Secondary Healthcare Initiative for Service Delivery Transformation (ASSIST) Project for India is to strengthen management capacity, access to, and quality of the secondary healthcare system in Assam. The project comprises of three components. The first component, strengthened management capacity of health systems at state, district, and facility level consists of following sub-components: (i) internal performance agreements (IPAs) to strengthen management capacity; and (ii) technical support and project operating costs to strengthen management capacity. The second component is improved access to and quality of essential services in existing secondary facilities. The third component, enhanced access to and structural quality of secondary care will invest in: (a) upgrading up to 10 community health center (CHCs) and sub-district hospitals (SDHs) to district hospital (DH) following national guidelines and provision of medical equipment and goods to enhance equitable access to secondary care, and (b) incremental operating costs of these newly upgraded facilities to improve structural quality of secondary care.

P178418.project_abstract: The development objective of the Tripura Rural Economic Growth and Service Delivery Project for India is to enhance connectivity and access to improved services and economic opportunities for tribal areas in Tripura. The project comprises of four components. The first component, strengthening foundations for economic development will support strengthening the foundations for economic development in the tribal blocks through an integrated set of investments in agricultural livelihoods and rural roads that can both ease access to markets and to schools. The second component, investing in services to develop human capital will support investments to increase the average years of educational attainment and enhanced preparedness for labor market transitions for students in the twenty-three (23) tribal blocks and especially in the twelve (12) priority tribal blocks. The third component, strengthening institutional capacities for service delivery objective is to support the strengthening of local institutions in the tribal blocks for improved service delivery. The fourth component, contingent emergency response component will support the provision of immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.

P177917.project_abstract: The development objective of the Multidisciplinary Education and Research Improvement in Technical Education Project for India is to improve quality, equity, and governance in technical education in select states and participating institutions. The project comprises of three components. The first component, improving quality and equity in participating institutions will focus on improving quality, employability, and equity in technical education in participating institutions in select states. It consists of following sub-components: (i) strengthening participating institutions to enhance student skills and employability; (ii) promoting equitable access; and (iii) promoting multidisciplinary education. The second component, improving research for better skills, entrepreneurship, and innovation will support better research and innovation outcomes, and address barriers faced by women in pursuing careers in research and innovation. It consists of following sub-components: (i) competitive research fund (CRF) and research hubs; (ii) developing incubation and innovation ecosystems; and (iii) institutional research and innovation capacity building. The third component, sector steering, including governance and internal and external quality assurance will support the states and institutions to build this capacity through peer exchange and training on a large scale through dedicated grant schemes. It consists of following sub-components: (i) quality assurance; (ii) governance; (iii) leadership training and academic careers; and (iv) project management and technical assistance.
P177917.project_name: Multidisciplinary Education and Research Improvement in Technical Education

P177876.project_abstract: The Project consists of the following components:- Component A: Strengthening community-based institutions(a)	Developing WUAs for new schemes. The component will, among other things, sensitize, mobilize, and establish new WUAs and support them in developing their skills and competencies to plan, operate, and manage irrigation schemes. This will include establishing governance procedures and social accountability mechanisms, developing equitable and sustainable water sharing and utilization systems, and developing as well as implementing their respective Scheme Cluster Development Management Plans (SCDMPs).(b)	Strengthening WUAs for existing schemes. The component will, among other things, map and assess WUAs’ performance; recommend and implement organizational strengthening activities; and design and deliver core training modules on operationalizing women’s representation, leadership skills, decision-making in WUAs, and social audits tools. It will include capacity building activities on governance, O&M of irrigation services, systems building for accounting and record keeping, social accountability, and sustainable water sharing and utilization.(c)	Establishing internal and external links. The component will, among other things, facilitate vertical integration of WUAs to function as collective; build capacity of WUAs on management and entrepreneurship through exposure visits, trade affairs, and structured training; provide targeted training and capacity building to strengthen management capabilities of women members in WUAs; and formalize links between WUAs and farmer producer organizations (FPOs).- Component B: Minor irrigation servicesThe component will improve access to water for irrigation, fisheries, and other livelihood activities through developing minor irrigation scheme clusters, including check dams (of less than 5 m in height in small streams), small-scale storage structures (ponds ranging from 400 to 4,000 m2), creek rehabilitation (up to 1.5 km), open dug wells, and tube wells; and scaling up water efficiency technologies, such as  improved conveyance and application systems and irrigation scheduling informed by soil moisture measurements.- Component C: Agricultural support services(a)	Agricultural crops. The component will invest in providing agricultural advisory services for field crops that are demand driven. The activities will include promoting efficient water management, high-yielding crop varieties, better agronomic practices, integrated soil fertility and nutrient management, integrated pest management and organic farming techniques, and other good agricultural practices.(b)	Horticulture. The component will support farmers in participating in fruit, vegetable, and floriculture supply chains that are of higher value than field crops. It will include carrying out farmers’ risk profiling, providing advisory services on good agricultural practices and innovative technologies, such as managing soil fertility and pests, formulating buyback arrangements and other contract farming in partnership with agribusiness companies, and promoting precision farming. It will also support WUAs in procuring critical inputs such as hybrid seeds and planting materials and piloting post-harvest facilities for grading, packing, branding, storing, and transporting produce. (c)	Aquaculture. The component will promote aquaculture through demonstrating and distributing modern technology practices, such as use of fish feed formulated with locally available ingredients, fingerling production and supply, cage fish culture, and culture-cum-capture models. It will also promote fish storage, transportation, and marketing. Inland fish production in tanks, ponds, and other inland water bodies can provide alternate livelihood to landless and marginal farmers.  - Component D: Project management and technical support (a)	Project implementation and coordination. The component will provide technical assistance, carry out training, acquire equipment, and finance incremental operating costs to strengthen the State Project Management Unit (SPMU) and District Project Management Units (DPMUs) to implement the Project, including modern facilities for adva   nced planning and execution.(b)	Organizational development. The component will provide technical assistance to the DWRID to institutionalize the best practices in implementation arrangements, processes, and design standards, including by establishing a cell for WUA development and support and a cell on planning and monitoring.
